To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the phase behavior of a SW fluid can be described by a unique equation of SAFT VR with a single parameter that can be related to the range parameter of SW.
a crossover treatment of the SAFT equation of state is presented which allows the prediction of the phase behavior for a wide range of conditions with only a single parameter.
we have developed a simple and accurate equation of state for chain and associative systems based on the SAFT VR equation of state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of an improved equation of state for chain and associatively interacting fluids that can be applied over the full range of temperature and pressure.
the application of the RG method to the SAFT VR equation of state for chain and associative systems.
the development of an accurate equation of state for the prediction of the phase behavior and critical properties of fluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RG method has proven to be a very useful tool in improving the predictions in the critical region.

the new approach is a significant improvement over the original White and Prausnitz treatment and provides an accurate description of the critical region and of the phase behavior far from the critical point.

the new equation of state provides an excellent prediction of phase behavior of chain fluids and of the critical region of associating fluids, and it is able to predict the critical properties of associating fluids with a unique fitted parameter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have extended the range of the SAFT equation to include the critical region.
the SAFT VR equation of state can be extended by a simple and straightforward method to account for the effects of density fluctuations of all wavelengths.
the new method provides accurate phase diagrams for associating and nonassociating fluids over a large range of conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new RG treatment is very accurate and can be easily applied to SAFT.
a simple RG approach can be used to obtain accurate predictions of the critical properties of chain and associative systems using only the parameters of the classical SAFT VR equation of state.
the RG method can be implemented into a SAFT type of equation of state with the use of a single adjustable parameter.
